subject: Cognitive Science
title: Elaborative Interrogation
description: A quick, practical guide to Elaborative Interrogation.

hook.text: Read a fact and move on? You'll forget it. Ask "why is this true?" and suddenly it sticks.

buildup.text: Elaborative interrogation means generating explanations for facts rather than passively reading them.

discovery.text: Asking "why" connects new information to things you already know, creating more retrieval routes.

twist.text: It works best when you already have some background knowledge. Beginners may struggle to explain why.

climax.text: The effort of generating an answer is what makes it effective. Easy answers don't build strong traces.

quiz.question: What makes elaborative interrogation effective?
options: Generating explanations connects new info to existing knowledge

details.summary: Elaborative interrogation is asking why and how questions about material being studied. Instead of just reading that copper conducts electricity, ask why copper is a good conductor. This simple technique forces connection to prior knowledge and produces deeper encoding than passive reading.
details.whyItMatters: Elaborative interrogation is one of the most effective study strategies with minimal effort. A simple why question transforms passive reading into active learning.
takeaways: Asking why and how during study deepens understanding
It forces connections between new and existing knowledge
Minimal additional effort produces significant learning gains

faq.question: How effective is elaborative interrogation compared to rereading?
faq.answer: Far more effective. Studies consistently show that asking why questions produces better retention than rereading, highlighting, or summarizing. The technique works because it activates relevant prior knowledge and creates meaningful connections, producing deeper encoding with minimal extra effort.

faq.question: When does elaborative interrogation work best?
faq.answer: It works best when you have enough prior knowledge to generate reasonable answers. Complete beginners may struggle to explain why. The technique is most powerful for learners with moderate knowledge who can connect new facts to what they already know. Some background knowledge is needed.
